summary.headline: Mold-Tek Q2 FY27: sales volume up 10.1% YoY and EBITDA per kg of INR46.5 vs ~INR39 a year ago, with EBITDA up about 36%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 volume growth of 10.1% YoY and profit growth of about 36%, with EBITDA per kg rising to INR46.5 from roughly INR39. Pharma volumes rose 26.3% and food and FMCG 23.7%, while lubricant packs fell 12.3% after losing clients to input issues at private lube companies. Management said October 2026 was the strongest month so far in the quarter and reiterated a double-digit volume target for FY27 and a 50,000+ tonne volume goal next year. Capex is being scaled down to about INR75-80 crore, with management guiding to debt reduction by year end.

financial_highlights.change: H1 volume growth about 8%, up from 7% in Q1
vs ~INR39 in Q2 last year, about 18% higher
EBITDA absolute up ~30% YoY; H1 EBITDA up 23% H1 on H1; PBT up ~35% YoY
vs INR40.6 in H1 last year
H1 pharma turnover about INR24 crore
decline about 15% in H1 per management
value up from 76%; volume up from prior year

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: Volume up 26.3% YoY; H1 turnover about INR24 crore, with a target of INR50+ crore for FY27 and INR70-75 crore for FY28. Management says 2-3 large clients are being added each quarter.

segments.name: Food and FMCG
segments.commentary: Volume up 23.7% YoY; Panipat plant adding clients, Iodex balm packs expected to start commercial production in Dec/Jan, and 3 new MNC products due Dec/Jan.

segments.name: Paints
segments.commentary: Volume up 8.6% YoY, value up 26%; Cheyyar plant taking southern orders, with management hoping for double-digit growth in H2.

segments.name: Lubricants
segments.commentary: Volume down 12.3% YoY after losing clients at private lube companies with input issues; management expects a decline every quarter this year.

segments.name: Qpack
segments.commentary: Growing into detergents; a new major-player order to begin supplies from end-November.

segments.name: Vibe (specialty closures JV)
segments.commentary: Seven products approved by Vibe; client trials in November, commercial molds in about 4 months, and commercial production around March-April. Management guides INR50-60 crore top line and ~30% EBITDA margin in about 2 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth target remains double-digit; H1 is ~8%, with management hoping for ~10% for the full year.
EBITDA per kg expected at INR45-46 range for the full year; long-term internal target of INR50 per kg over the next 2-3 years.
FY27 EBITDA target about INR250 crore vs INR173 crore last year; operating cash flow target about INR215 crore vs INR107 crore last year.
FY27 capex about INR75-80 crore (INR60 crore spent in first 7 months); expected net cash surplus with debt likely reducing by year end.
Next year capacity to reach about 70,000 tonnes from 66,900; volume target 50,000-51,000 tonnes vs about 46,000-47,000 tonnes this year.
Finance cost planned at 4.5-4.7% of revenue for FY27, expected to ease to 4-4.2% if raw material prices fall.
capex_capacity: Capacity about 66,900 tonnes, with additional machines expected to take it to about 68,000-69,000; management targets around 70,000 by start of FY28. Management says utilisation above 75% is not workable.
Capex for FY27 about INR75-80 crore; investment in Vibe phase 1 about INR10-15 crore for molds and machines, sufficient for INR40-50 crore turnover.
Ophthalmic eye-dropper packs: molds ordered, ready by January, trials about 2 months, commercial production from about April-May next year in 3 sizes; this is being built in Sultanpur B block.
New land purchased at Sultanpur registered only a few days before the call; construction not yet started, with use for auto-injector pens or semiconductor trays yet to be decided.
Robots: about 130-140 currently, with machine count above 200.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices up about 60% over the last 6 months; management says customers are accepting pass-through of raw material increases under long-standing contracts.
Management says competitors are not being forced out by higher crude prices because they can pass on costs if they are reliable suppliers.
Exports are under pressure from higher freight costs; US stent and battery packs are recovering, and an Egyptian pharma importer is due to visit in early December.
Paint industry growth is about 8-10% per management; paint tonnage is largely stagnant while food, FMCG and pharma add more value per tonne.
October 2026 described as the strongest month of the quarter so far in month-on-month terms.

qa_highlights.question: Will paint volume growth continue, and is there any backlog shipping in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said paint volume grew 8.6% (value +26%), with the industry at 8-10%. Cheyyar is adding southern orders and volume could approach double digits in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA per kg stay at INR45-50 for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to hold INR45-46 for the full year, with Q3 starting strongly. Last year's full-year figure was INR40.7.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for lubricants and normalised volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Decline reflects clients at private lube companies with input issues; management expects a decline in every quarter this year rather than growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines for auto-injector pens and semiconductor trays?
qa_highlights.answer: Pens depend on a partner or patent-owner deal, with trading possibly starting first and no numbers within 2-3 months. Semiconductor trays are seen contributing from FY28-FY29 and are at the discussion stage with 3 companies.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash flow and free cash flow is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets operating cash flow of about INR215 crore vs INR107 crore last year, with capex about INR75-80 crore and a cash surplus expected.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Vibe investment be funded and sized?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 investment is about INR10-15 crore for molds and machinery, with machines largely fungible across products. Commitment depends on firm orders expected by end of this year.

risks_watch: Lubricant volume decline is expected to continue each quarter, given the loss of clients at private lube companies.
Raw material inflation tied to crude and West Asia tensions; management expects no quick decline, keeping finance cost at 4.5-4.7% of revenue.
Vibe, pharma and semiconductor ramp-up depends on client trials, commercial molds and partner deals (JV or patent), with timing uncertain.
Export growth constrained by freight costs.
Land registration at Sultanpur was delayed for about a year, which could affect timelines for the new site.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and pharma/FMCG growth, with specific numbers. Cautious and vague on timelines for the auto-injector pens, semiconductor trays and exports, which management repeatedly described as long-dated.

growth.why: Management holds FY27 double-digit volume growth (H1 ~8%, targeting ~10%) and FY27 EBITDA target of ~INR250 crore vs INR173 crore, backed by capacity rising from 66,900 t to ~70,000 t by start of FY28, pharma and food/FMCG volume growth, and new Vibe and ophthalmic products from around March-May; lubricant volume down 12.3% is a drag and capex is being cut to ~INR75-80 crore.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA per kg at INR46.5 in Q2 vs ~INR39 a year ago, and management guides INR45-46 for full FY27 vs INR40.7 last year, with raw material pass-through accepted under contracts.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q4 FY27 to start of FY28
rows.why: Capacity goes from ~66,900 t to ~70,000 t by start of FY28, with additional machines adding ~6,000-7,000 t and the work already under construction.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 volume growth is ~8% and management still targets ~10% for FY27, with pharma +26.3% and food/FMCG +23.7%, offset by lubricants -12.3%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is ~67% and capex is being cut to INR75-80 crore for FY27, with no new major plant guided, though a Vibe phase-1 spend of INR10-15 crore is already committed and depends on firm orders.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: October was the strongest month of the quarter so far and management is holding FY27 targets, but volume guidance is held at double digits rather than raised, with H1 at ~8%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Lubricant volume is expected to fall every quarter, and finance cost of 4.5-4.7% of revenue depends on raw material prices that management expects will not fall quickly.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Iodex balm packs and 3 new MNC products are due Dec/Jan, Qpack detergent supply starts end-November, Vibe commercial production is around March-April, and ophthalmic packs are due April-May.

rows.label: Semiconductor trays and auto-injector pens
rows.why: Semiconductor trays are at discussion stage with 3 companies and expected from FY28-FY29, while pens depend on a partner or patent deal with no numbers within 2-3 months.

rows.label: Pharma turnover to INR50+ crore FY27
rows.why: H1 pharma turnover is about INR24 crore and management adds 2-3 large clients each quarter, with FY28 target of INR70-75 crore.

rows.label: Debt reduction by year end
rows.why: FY27 operating cash flow target is about INR215 crore vs INR107 crore last year, with capex of INR75-80 crore, leaving a net cash surplus.

tone.note: Management was confident on EBITDA per kg of INR45-46, pharma and FMCG growth and deleveraging, and cautious and vague on timelines for auto-injector pens, semiconductor trays and exports; analysts focused on the Q&A on lubricants, cash flow and Vibe funding.
